reviews.reason: The printed unit is present on p90, but the difficult sequence after 'inexhaustible' needs exact diplomatic verification. Its baseline asterisk and raised notes 5–7 must not be conflated. The supplied repeated forms cannot be approved merely because both input fields agree. The English notes are also substantially misanchored.
reviews.footnote_changes: Replace the unsupported 'OCR witness' explanation with an edition-specific account of the printed reading and apparatus. Anchor the textual difficulty at 'around it'; the fountain alternative at 'spring'; the holy-ones alternative at 'the holy'; and the non-failing alternative at 'inexhaustible'. Delete redundant previous-rendering notes d and e. Do not cluster unrelated notes after 'wisdom'.

reviews.reason: The English broadly represents the printed unit, including the naming and Head-of-Days clauses. Both notes are attached to the wrong expression. The baseline asterisk before the Son-of-Man expression is distinct from raised apparatus note 18.
reviews.suggested_text: And at that hour that Son of Man was named[a] in the presence of the Lord of Spirits, and his name was before the Head of Days[b].
reviews.footnote_changes: Retain note a at 'was named' and note b at 'Head of Days'. If discussing the word order of the Son-of-Man expression, identify the alternatives in p90 note 18 rather than silently normalizing them.

reviews.reason: The exact form of the signs word requires checking: the printed sequence appears to have ወትእምር rather than the supplied ወታእምር. Apparatus notes 21–24 belong to this construction. The current English and notes give incompatible groupings of sun, signs, and heavenly stars.
reviews.footnote_changes: Move the presence alternative to the final 'before the Lord of Spirits'. Remove or rewrite note b: it currently treats the disputed grouping as settled and is not a cross-reference. Do not present note c's regrouping as an equivalent previous rendering without explaining its textual or syntactic basis.

reviews.reason: The staff, support, light, and hope clauses are represented. The English notes are misplaced. The printed asterisk before the light expression must remain distinct from raised note 28; apparatus variants must not be substituted without identification.
reviews.suggested_text: He will be a staff for the righteous, so that they may lean on him and not fall; and he will be the light of the nations[a], and he will be hope for those who are troubled in heart[b].
reviews.footnote_changes: Place note a at 'light of the nations' and note b at 'troubled in heart'. Delete the redundant previous-rendering note c. Keep any discussion of the readings in notes 25–30 separate from lexical alternatives.

reviews.reason: The printed praise and blessing verbs have expressed pronominal objects, which the English should preserve. The dry-land note is misplaced. Raised note 35 within the final phrase is apparatus, not part of the Ethiopic wording.
reviews.suggested_text: All who dwell upon the dry land[a] shall fall down and bow before him, and they shall praise him and bless him and sing to the Lord of Spirits.
reviews.footnote_changes: Move note a to 'dry land'. If explaining the relationship between 'him' and 'the Lord of Spirits', distinguish translation of the printed object suffixes from interpretation; do not silently remove them.

reviews.reason: This unit crosses from the last text line of p90 to the first text line of p91. Its scope is correctly extended across that boundary, but the exact endings of the chosen/hidden forms are not sufficiently secure for source approval. The asterisk before the creation verb is editorial; the raised numerals refer to apparatus. The supplied terminal punctuation is not a diplomatic reproduction of the printed double separator.
reviews.suggested_text: For this reason, he was chosen and hidden before him[a] before the world was created, and forever[b].
reviews.footnote_changes: Move note a to 'before him' and note b to 'forever'; delete redundant note c. Where relevant, identify p91 note 2's omission of the creation verb and note 3's additions after the eternity expression as witness readings, not the selected main text.

reviews.reason: The supplied source omits the printed ለ immediately before the life expression. Raised note 13 is attached there, and the apparatus says 'a omits.' Thus the current source silently follows an omission rather than the selected printed reading. 'Their life came to be' does not transparently represent the retained preposition. The opening English also supplies 'him' without identifying that interpretive supplementation.
reviews.footnote_changes: Restore and explain the life-clause preposition before settling its English syntax; a provisional literal rendering is 'and by his will it was for their life.' Identify witness a's omission explicitly if that reading is adopted. Move the portion note to 'portion of the righteous' and the life-clause note to that clause. Delete 'wisdom was poured out' as an unsupported alternative to the displayed main-text verb. Explain any supplied object 'him' at the opening.

reviews.reason: The opening is not faithfully represented by በ*ዝንቱ … ክኑ. The print has a corruption sign resembling a dagger, not the supplied asterisk, and its demonstrative appears as እንቱ; the verb appears as ኮኑ, not ክኑ. Note 15 explicitly calls the transmitted expression corrupt and distinguishes manuscript readings from correction. Exact transcription of the marked opening remains held rather than silently emended.
reviews.footnote_changes: Replace note a's merely 'compressed' explanation with the documented textual corruption. Distinguish the printed corrupt demonstrative, the m t β reading, and the proposed correction to ዝንቱ. Explain the verbal form and tense rather than treating 'shall be humbled' as mechanically established. Move the dry-land note to 'dry land' and the works note to 'works of their hands'. Delete the unsupported previous-rendering note about the humble being put to shame.

reviews.reason: The supplied stars after ወ and ለ do not correspond to baseline asterisks at those positions: the print has raised apparatus references 21 and 23. The exact first-person verb must also be checked against note 25 rather than normalized silently. Note 26 reports an editorially significant placement of a five-word sequence, and note 29 reports a conjunction supplied by all manuscripts.
reviews.footnote_changes: Delete 'of the chosen ones I saw them', which is not supported as an alternative by the displayed apparatus. Preserve 'my' when describing the opening literally. Move the stubble alternative to 'straw' and the trace explanation to 'no trace'. Delete the unsubstantiated past-tense previous rendering. If explaining the printed arrangement, disclose note 26: m omits the sequence, while the other manuscripts transpose it after 'water'. Distinguish note 29's manuscript conjunction from the editor's printed wording.

reviews.reason: The canonical source and English are truncated. Printed unit 10 continues from p91 through all four text lines above XLIX on p92. It includes falling without rising, the hand/raising clause, denial of the Lord of Spirits and his Anointed, and the final blessing. The expanded candidate restores that scope but is not thereby exact-source approved. Its opening ወ*በ* conflates a raised reference with an asterisk; the hand-clause forms and other exact glyphs still require verification.
reviews.suggested_text: And on the day of their affliction, rest shall come upon the earth. Before them they shall fall and shall not rise; there is no one to take them by the hand and raise them, because they have denied the Lord of Spirits and his Anointed. And blessed be the name of the Lord of Spirits.
reviews.footnote_changes: Treat the suggested English as provisional, especially the hand clause. Replace note a's reference to the nonexistent main-text word 'distress'; move note b to the rest clause. Disclose the p92 apparatus rather than hiding a witness choice: note 1 varies the opening before-them expression; note 2 records m's altered fall form and q's omission; note 3 records m's alternative in the rising clause; notes 4–5 vary the no-one and hand expressions; notes 6 and 9 concern the Spirits form. Note 7 says g omits the Anointed expression and the following four words through the final Spirits expression, so that omission must not govern an unlabelled translation of the printed edition. Note 8 records 't u omit against m q, β' at its marked locus; do not expand that into an unsupported omission of the entire blessing. Retain the printed continuation unless a different witness is explicitly selected.
